cost.note: From listings, not deeds — and here that is legitimate: the condominium fee is a fact about the building, not an asking position. We do not show IPTU yet: listings quote it monthly or yearly with nothing marking which, and a median over mixed units would be exactly the invented number this site exists to call out.

entry.head: on top of the bid
entry.note: The commission is the winner's by law and custom; ITBI is levied on the hammer price; deed and registry follow the state fee table — the tilde is honest, the exact figure steps with the value band. Not counted: renovation, eviction if occupied, and the property's debts when the sale is not judicial.
entry.note.direct: Caixa direct sale: no auctioneer, no commission. ITBI is levied on the price; deed and registry follow the state fee table. Not counted: renovation, eviction if occupied, and any condominium debt — in an extrajudicial sale it can stay with the buyer.
entry.note.extrajud: Note: in an extrajudicial auction (Law 9.514) condominium debt can follow the property — the CPC protection only applies in court sales.
foot.note: Data: ITBI, Caixa, listing portals. Updated {date}. This is not investment advice and not a valuation for a transaction — read the edital and the matrícula before the auction.
foot.privacy: We count visits without cookies and collect no personal data. In your browser we keep only the language, city and theme you picked.

home.h1: Property auctions {br} — are they really cheap?
home.lede: The discount the platforms advertise is measured against the bank's appraisal. We measure against the price identical properties actually fetch at the hammer — and where there are no comparable sales nearby, we show no number at all.
home.more: No estimate yet, but already with real ITBI prices per district: {links}
home.why.p: A bank appraisal is a valuation nobody paid. We start from ITBI — the tax that only exists once a deed has been signed — and from {deals} sales that actually happened. Then we carry that price down to where the auction ends, because a winning bidder does not pay asking price.
honest.base: The register's price is an upper bound. The city records the larger of the declared value and its own appraisal, so the medians can sit slightly above what was really paid.
honest.basis: We don't price a lot from listings — a listing is what the seller is asking. We take {deals} real ITBI sales and {listings} listings nearby and bring them down to the price auctions in this city actually end at.
honest.basis.market: We don't value lots in this city yet: we haven't measured the chain down to the hammer here. What we do have is {deals} real deals from the {year} ITBI register — the district prices come from them.
honest.chain: Borrowed chain. {why}, so {what}. That's an estimate by analogy, and we say so rather than hide it.
honest.chain.auction: and the hammer's discount to the market from {city}
honest.chain.premium: we took the asking premium over sales from {city}
honest.chain.why.none: This city doesn't publish its own ITBI
honest.chain.why.some: The city does have its own sales, but publishes no finished auctions to show a hammer price
honest.head: The head of the ranking is the tail of our error. The higher a lot sits, the better the chance we simply overpriced the market right there.
honest.map: The map. The boundaries here come from {source}. {kind} A lot lands on the map by its coordinates, not by the name of its district.
honest.map.exact: That is the legal boundary, not a reconstruction of ours.
honest.map.inferred: It isn't a legal boundary but where the addresses actually stand; along an unbuilt edge it can diverge noticeably from the official one.
honest.withheld: Where there are too few comparable sales nearby we don't show an estimate. Blank space is more honest than an invented number.

lot.note.court: A judicial auction: under art. 130, sole paragraph, of the CTN and art. 908, § 1, of the CPC, IPTU and condomínio debts are transferred onto the sale price and do not pass to the buyer — even where the edital says otherwise.

mkt.note: Source: the city's own ITBI — the tax that is only paid once a deed has been signed. Not an asking price and not a bank appraisal: this is what changed hands. The comparison is against the city median for the same kind of property and the same year, because the register's values are nominal and comparing across years would measure inflation.
mkt.note.base: This city's register keeps the larger of the declared price and the municipal appraisal, so the medians can sit slightly above what was paid.

why.city_only: The address in the notice placed the property in a city, not on a street. A ring drawn at the city centre compares this lot with central properties three to five times dearer than the outer districts where auction stock actually sits — that is how 80% “discounts” get manufactured. We would rather give no number.
why.conf.appraisal_gap: The official appraisal and the market disagree too sharply. With the two references fighting, a verdict from us would be picking a side with nothing to pick it on.
why.conf.no_appraisal: The notice carries no official appraisal, so the second reference we check ours against is missing.
why.conf.price_gap: The opening bid sits so far below the appraisal that the gap is not a discount but a sign the listing describes something else — debts, occupancy, or an area other than the registered one.
why.conf.restricted: The lot carries a resale restriction (social housing or an equivalent clause): a market price does not apply to a buyer who cannot sell at market.
why.conf.rights: What is on sale is rights over the property, not the property: the winner joins a legal queue, not a deed.
why.h: Why there is no estimate here
why.hint: For scale: properties advertised in {bairro} — of any kind and size — average {area} m² and ask {m2} per m² ({n} active listings).
why.hint.city: For scale: the listings we hold in {city}, of any kind, ask {m2} per m² on average.
why.no_area: The auction notice never published the property's size. Our whole calculation starts from price per m², so with no metres there is no divisor — and an invented number is exactly what this site exists to call out.
why.no_comps: We looked for listings of the same kind and size at 500 m, 1, 2, 5, 10, 20 and 30 km. Even at 30 km there is no sample big enough for an honest median.
why.no_coords: The address in the notice could not be located, even approximately.
why.no_type: “{tipo}” has no equivalent on the listing portals: a parking space, a plot of land, an odd commercial unit. Comparing it with flats is the mistake that once put a garage space at the top of a discount list.
why.ring: The nearest comparable listings are {ring} m away. We only call it a verdict when it rests on sales within 1 km — further out is already a different piece of the city.
why.wide: Nothing comparable stood nearby, so the radius was opened step by step out to {km} km, where {n} listings appeared. At that distance this is no longer your district: any market figure on this page is context, not a valuation, and it enters no ranking on this site.
why.wide.h: We had to widen the search to {km} km
